bull.b: Robust Phase 1a structural/functional gains and markedly lower plasma Cmax suggest TH103 may offer longer intraocular durability and favorable safety. Durable dosing advantages and clear biological differentiation can establish sustainable competitive positioning in nAMD and guide Phase 3 dose selection.

Very low reported debt relative to equity limits near-term interest and solvency pressure, preserving flexibility for financing choices. This balance-sheet characteristic reduces bankruptcy risk and supports strategic optionality while the company funds development prior to commercial revenues.

Hiring a CFO with capital markets and biotech equity experience enhances fundraising execution and investor communications. Coupled with an interim accounting lead and clear governance moves, this improves operational continuity and increases probability of more effective future financing and transaction execution.

bear.b: Sustained, sizable operating cash burn and continued pre-revenue status create a structural reliance on external capital. Unless clinical progress is rapid, the company faces recurring financing events that can dilute shareholders and stress execution if market access or terms worsen over multiple funding rounds.

Business is concentrated on clinical-stage therapeutics (notably TH103). This single-asset orientation means commercial and valuation outcomes are highly binary; a setback in trials or regulatory review would materially impair future prospects and heighten funding and strategic risks.

Declining equity and past episodes of negative equity reflect value erosion and prior funding strain. This reduces the cushion against losses, complicates future financings, can force dilutive capital raises, and signals higher governance and solvency risk relative to peers with more stable equity bases.
